label: copy-phase input token i (fed-back i), from the 2nd copy input on
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and only when the input is the letter i (the model fed its own earlier output i back in). It never fires on i during the original phase, on the delimiter, or on any other token. On input i alone it has recall 1.0 and precision 0.77. Most false positives are the first copy input (recall_idx 1, where the input is orig(0)); there the feature is mostly off or weak, so excluding that step gives dev F1 0.92 and mass recall 0.99. Magnitude: strongest when i is orig(1) fed back at recall_idx 2 (37% of mass, top activations around 4), especially after a non-i orig(0). A second consecutive i fires about half as strongly. Activation gets weaker, and more often fails to fire, for i at later copy positions. Leading i in the sequence (first_tok=i) gives only weak activation.

issues: Reproduced the test scores exactly: P 0.899, R 0.954, F1 0.925, mass recall 0.988. The bare (phase==2)&(in_tok==i) predicate gets recall 1.0 and mass recall 1.0, so the feature never fires outside copy-phase i (0 activations in original phase, on the delimiter, and on every other in_tok).

The false positives follow a position gradient, not a separate class. Precision by recall_idx on test: 0.999 at 2, 0.994 at 3, 0.974 at 4, 0.84 at 5, 0.67 at 6, 0.69 at 7, 0.72 at 8. The explanation already says this ('weaker and more often absent at later copy positions'). Cutting at recall_idx<=4 gives F1 0.79 and requiring the first copy-phase i gives F1 0.90, so neither beats the original. No clean cause showed up for the late drop: L, to_go, in_count and digit prev_tok each sit around 0.70-0.85.

Minor: repeated i is weaker. A second consecutive i (prev_tok==i) has precision 0.70 and a later copy-phase i (n_seen > in_count) has 0.72, against 0.92 for the first copy-phase i. This fits the 'second consecutive i about half as strong' claim and is a small fraction of the mass.
The recall_idx 1 exclusion is justified: there the precision is 0.19 and the mass is 1.2%. The missed activations in the misses output are all weak (0.02-0.10 relative) i inputs at recall_idx 1.

The magnitude claims check out. recall_idx 2 holds 37.4% of the mass and the max activation is 4.15. At recall_idx 2 with a non-i orig(0), precision is 0.9996 and mass is 36%. When orig(0) is i, the mass share is below the step share, so activation there is weaker as claimed.
